items.title: Abbey Lincoln — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: he said to me on the phone, 'Abby, what do you want to do?'... he signed me for three albums.

ctx.x: How did you -- when you did the album in '56 with the Benny Carter arrangement and Marty Page and Benny Carter, -­

That was Bob Russell who did that. It's always been for me like that. After Bob, it was Max and now there's Jean-Philippe Allard, somebody to help me to think because I don't know these musicians. I didn't know who Marty Page was or, I mean, I heard his name, but I wouldn't have thought to ask Benny Carter to do this.
How did this -- when you got these arrangements, when you started to work on that, was it different from what you'd done in the past musically?
